function.name: crash_list
function.description: List every crash report, one line each: its ID, fingerprint, how many times it happened, the version that crashed, the function inside remind where it happened, and the panic message, cut short. Reports with the same fingerprint usually share a cause, but check. Start here.

function.name: crash_read
function.description: Read one crash report: when and how often it happened, the panic, the request being served, and the stack. By default the stack shows only remind's own frames, with file and line; set full for every frame. Log lines are in crash_logs.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

full.description: show every stack frame, not just remind's

function.name: crash_search
function.description: Search every crash report for text, ignoring case: panic messages, request paths and bodies, stacks, and log lines. Lists each match with the report's ID and where it was found.

query.description: text to look for, such as a function name, a path, or words from a panic

function.name: crash_logs
function.description: Read the log lines remind wrote just before a crash.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: crash_goroutines
function.description: Summarize the goroutine dump of a stuck request: goroutines with identical stacks are grouped and counted, so a dump of thousands reads as a few groups. Use it for reports of kind stuck.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: code_list
function.description: List the files under a directory of remind's source, with how many lines each has. Use it to find your way around; use code_search to find where something is defined.

dir.description: a directory such as "store"; empty lists everything

function.name: code_read
function.description: Read part of a file of remind's source, with line numbers. Shows at most 200 lines at a time; ask for a range with start and end. Read a file before you change it.

path.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

start.description: the first line to show; default 1

end.description: the last line to show; default 200 lines after start

function.name: code_search
function.description: Search remind's Go files for a regular expression and list the matching lines with file and line number. Use it to find where a function is defined or called.

pattern.description: a Go regular expression, such as func \(s \*Store\) Get

dir.description: limit the search to this directory

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run go test on remind's code, as it is now, and report failed tests, build errors, and each package's result. Run one package while you work; run ./... before you finish.

package.description: a package pattern, such as ./store or ./...

run.description: run only tests matching this regular expression, such as ^TestGetDeleted$

function.name: code_patch
function.description: Change a file by replacing one piece of text, or create a new file, such as a test, by leaving old empty. Read a file with code_read before changing it, and copy old exactly from what you read. After a change, the package and its tests are compiled, and you see the result.

path.description: the file to change, such as store/store.go

old.description: text copied exactly from the file, appearing in it once; empty to create a new file

new.description: the text to put in its place, or the new file's contents

function.name: issue_search
function.description: Search the open issues in the issue tracker, by words or by fingerprint; with neither, list them all. Issues that contain more of the words come first. Check here before filing, since a crash may already be filed, perhaps by a person, with no fingerprint and in other words.

query.description: words to look for in titles and bodies, such as parseBearer index out of range

function.name: issue_file
function.description: File a new issue for a crash group, once you know its cause. Search the open issues first; don't file a problem that is already filed. File one issue per cause.

title.description: one line naming the problem, such as "store.Get returns a deleted reminder"

body.description: the cause, the evidence, the fix, and the reports it covers

fingerprint.description: the crash group's fingerprint, from crash_list

function.name: issue_comment
function.description: Add a comment to an issue, such as new crash reports that match one already filed.

body.description: the comment, such as new reports of the same crash

function.name: submit_diagnosis
function.description: Finish the job: submit one diagnosis per crash group. Call it once, at the end, after filing an issue for each new cause. For status fixed, the reproducer test must fail on the original code and pass on yours; this is checked.

groups.description: one entry per crash group; every report belongs to exactly one

reports.description: the IDs of every report in the group

root_cause.description: where the code is wrong, which may not be where it crashed

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

evidence.description: why this is the cause: what you read and ran

reproducer.description: the test you wrote that fails before the fix; leave out for already_fixed and duplicate

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

fix.description: what you changed, for status fixed

issue.description: the issue you filed, for status fixed or needs_human

duplicate.description: for status duplicate: the open issue it duplicates

message.content: I can already see likely causes for several of these. Let me read the auth package, the API routing, and the rest of snooze, plus existing tests.
message.reasoning:
Now I can see the bugs:

**Bug 1: duration.Parse with empty string** (fp_34f681, cr_b73dbe, x2)
`duration.Parse("")` → `s[len(s)-1]` = `s[-1]` → index out of range [-1]. Triggered by `POST /v1/reminders/rem_0001/snooze` with body `{"for":""}`. In snooze, `duration.Parse(req.For)` is called with empty string. Wait — does snooze validate that For is non-empty? Let me check lines 200-223. Actually the crash is at duration/duration.go:29 via api/reminders.go:197 (snooze). So `req.For` was "". Fix: in Parse, handle empty string (return error "missing unit" or empty duration error). The proper fix: check `if s == ""` return error. Root cause is duration.Parse not handling empty input. Category: out_of_range.

**Bug 2: store.Get returns nil, nil for deleted reminder** (fp_4828a6, cr_6265c5)
In `Store.Get`, when reminder exists but is Deleted, it sets `r = nil` but doesn't set err. So Get returns (nil, nil). Then in `owned`, `err` is nil, so it proceeds to `rem.UserID` → nil pointer deref. Triggered by POST /v1/reminders/rem_0003/done after rem_0003 was deleted at 14:12:35. Fix: in Get, when deleted, set err = ErrNotFound (return nil, ErrNotFound). Root cause: store.(*Store).Get. Category: nil_value.

**Bug 3: store.List slice bounds out of range** (fp_6a569c, cr_76768c + cr_ed4938)
`GET /v1/reminders?offset=20` with only 2 (then 1) reminders. `List(userID, 20, limit)`: `out` has len 2; `end := min(offset+limit, len(out))` = min(20+limit, 2) = 2; `out[20:2]` → slice bounds out of range [20:2]. Fix: clamp offset: if offset > len(out), return empty. E.g.:

```go
if offset >= len(out) {
    return nil
}
end := min(offset+limit, len(out))
return out[offset:end]
```

Note cr_ed4938 shows [20:1] — user had 1 non-deleted reminder after deleting one. Same cause. Category: out_of_range.

**Bug 4: api.export nil pointer** (fp_86f99d, cr_d80efa)
`a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)` — wait, crash at api/users.go:104 which is `rems := a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)`. Hmm, nil pointer deref there. What's nil? `a.Store`? Hmm. Wait — but stats at api/users.go:117 also crashed with nil deref: `for _, rem := range a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)`.

Hmm, both crash in `a.Store.List` call... but the nil deref — what could be nil there? `a.Store` is a field of API. If a.Store were nil, then calling List would deref nil. But other endpoints use a.Store fine... Actually wait, maybe the user is nil? No, `auth.UserFrom(r.Context())` — if that returned nil, `u.ID` would panic. Line 104 is `rems := a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)`. Hmm, the panic line is 104 for export and 117 for stats.

Wait, but List with offset=0 wouldn't panic. Unless... hmm, let me think. Actually maybe the issue is in List itself: `s.byUser[userID]`... no nil deref there.

Hold on — maybe `auth.UserFrom` returned nil for these users? Let me check auth package. Actually the crash function listed is `api.(*API).export` at users.go:104 and `api.(*API).stats` at users.go:117. The panic is nil pointer dereference. Possible nils at line 104: `a.Store` (if nil) or `u` (if nil). But line 104 is `rems := a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)` — if u is nil, u.ID panics; if a.Store is nil, calling method on nil pointer receiver — List has pointer receiver (*Store); calling a method on a nil *Store panics when the method dereferences s.mu... Actually calling s.mu.RLock() on nil s panics with nil pointer dereference.

But why would a.Store be nil for export/stats but not elsewhere? Hmm, wait. Maybe these are different users — usr_bo and usr_ana. Let me check: the export request UA is Safari (desktop, usr_ana?), stats UA is remind-ios (usr_bo?).

Hmm, maybe the issue is that `auth.UserFrom` returns nil for... no, then u.ID at line 103→104 would panic. Actually line 103 is `u := auth.UserFrom(r.Context())` and 104 is the List call. If u were nil, panic would be at line 104 too (evaluating u.ID inside the call at line 104)! Actually u.ID is evaluated at line 104 as part of the call expression. Hmm, but stack shows the panic in export at users.go:104. If u is nil, `u.ID` inside `a.Store.List(u.ID, ...)` — the panic would occur at line 104 when evaluating arguments. So possibly u is nil!

Why would u be nil? auth.UserFrom returns the user from context. If auth middleware didn't put a user in context... Let me read auth/auth.go. The stack shows auth.Require at auth/auth.go:23 in the handler chain (for reminders). For export/stats, the stack shows only server.accessLog and metrics.Instrument — no auth.Require frame! Interesting: cr_d80efa stack: `api.(*API).export` ← `server.accessLog` ← `metrics.Instrument`. No auth.Require! While reminders ones show auth.Require between the handler and accessLog.

So export and stats routes are not wrapped in auth.Require! Then `auth.UserFrom(r.Context())` returns nil → panic at `u.ID`. Let me verify by reading auth/auth.go and api/api.go routes.

Let me also check whether UserFrom can return nil: it probably does `u, _ := ctx.Value(userKey).(*User)` and returns u — nil if absent.

So bugs 4 and 5 (export, stats) might share a root cause: missing auth.Require on those routes → u nil → nil deref. But they have different fingerprints because different functions. Do they share a cause? Both are "missing auth middleware on /v1/me routes" — but wait, `/v1/me` worked for `me` and `updatePrefs` presumably... Let me read api/api.go to see route registration.

Also for markDone/owned: `owned` at line 144 `rem.UserID != u.ID` — rem is nil because Get returned (nil, nil) for deleted. That's bug 2. The root cause is store.Get returning nil, nil.

Alternatively the fix could be in owned to handle nil rem — but the root cause is Get's contract violation. Let me check Get's doc: "Get returns a reminder by ID. Deleted reminders are not returned." Returning (nil, nil) for deleted is the bug: err should be ErrNotFound.

Let me now read the remaining files: auth/auth.go, api/api.go, and rest of reminders.go (200-223), and store/store_test.go to see existing tests. Also duration/duration_test.go.

Let me batch: code_read auth/auth.go, api/api.go, api/reminders.go start=200, duration/duration_test.go, store/store_test.go.
